name: A scraped webpage's ordinary onload/onerror/onclick handlers and script tag (no dangerous call target)
notes: TODOS #54 FP guard. A fetch/scrape/browse-style MCP tool routinely returns raw webpage HTML verbatim, and real-world pages very commonly carry onload/onerror/onclick attributes and <script> tags for entirely ordinary reasons (image fallback, lazy init, analytics). None of these call a privileged MCP-client bridge or a process/eval primitive, so renderer-code-execution-in-response's dangerous-call-target gate must not fire on them. Found while designing the detector: a bare event-handler/script-tag presence check (as the TODO originally sketched) would have false-positived on nearly every scraped page.
